checks: A through-interior cut has positive section area and positive support height on both sides. The convex hull of its actual section with a farthest point is contained in the corresponding closed cap. Its volume is section area times perpendicular height divided by d.

For the optional marginal hypothesis, apply Gauss–Green to x−g. The new cut face contributes zero, and on the retained old boundary the integrand is h_{B−g} evaluated at the outer normal almost everywhere. The cutting plane meets the interior, so its intersection with the old boundary is the relative boundary of the cut section and has zero (d−1)-measure.

The negative normal in the section measure pairs the captured term with the reflected body −J and the complement with J. This is the surface-area representation with J repeated d−1 times. Without the representation assumption both support integrals still exist.

Positive weights force every captured remainder to vanish at equality. Each inscribed pyramid is compact and full dimensional, so strict containment would omit positive volume. Minkowski's first inequality gives the volume factor and its homothety equality condition.
